assumptions: Path from the S6 transit simulator run forward from the observed state with the current rudder and engine order held.
Hull footprint is a parametric planform from catalog LOA and beam centred on the reported position, rotated by heading.
Environment held constant over the horizon.
Corridor spread (when sampled): start position/heading/speed per the supplied one-sigma values; wind speed 15%, wind direction 10 deg, current speed 20%, current direction 15 deg (illustrative sd).

reasons.message: Hull forces are Clarke et al. (1983) regression derivatives plus assumed cross-flow drag and an MMG-style rudder; not identified or validated for any ship; not for navigation.
No propulsion, rudder or thruster data exist: T_max is calibrated to a public nominal maximum speed; engine lag, astern fraction, rudder size/rate and race are labeled assumptions.
Deep water assumed: no squat, shallow-water, bank or channel effects, no under-keel clearance check.
Vessels share one clock but exert no forces on each other; no collision or passing-distance check.
Input age 2 s (as_of - observed); environment age 1020 s.
An input is older than 300 s; the ship and conditions may have changed.
The transit start supports only forward surge from rest actuators: rudder starts at 0 and slews to the observed angle at the steering-gear rate.
No coastline data are wired: coastline clearance is not checked, so not clear, just unknown.
Illustrative spread of simple seeded perturbations; the S10 uncertainty model is not yet wired. Breach probability is a sample share, not calibrated. Samples use dt 1 s.

alternatives.label: Tug pushes the bow to port (270 deg relative)
